# Text Formatting

**wrap text in double asterisks to bold**

*wrap text in single asterisks to italicize*

***wrap text in triple to bold and italicize***

~~wrap text in double tildes to strikethrough~~

``` markdown

wrap inline rcode in single backticks to code...
2 + 2 + 2 + = `\{r} 2 + 2 + 2` *backslash is not needed, only used here to print
```

2 + 2 + 2 + = `\{r} 2 + 2 + 2`

# Loading libraries & Reading in data

This should be done at the top of your quarto doc, after YAML.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| echo: fenced
    
# load your libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(readxl)

# reading in data
# example: mydata <- read.csv("path/to/data.csv")

my_data <- mtcars
my_real_data <- read_excel("~/Downloads/TCRMP_SiteMetadata.xlsx")
# the ~/ tab went to my computer directory, a double period (../ tab) would take me to my project directory

head(my_real_data)
```

# inserting figures and figure captions

```{r}
#| label: fig-mpg
#| fig-cap: "Scatterplot of Car Weight vs. MPG"

ggplot(my_data, aes(x = wt, y = mpg))+
  geom_point() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "weight", y = "miles per gallon")
```

::: callout-tip
## Tip

notice how we labeled figure above with option #\| labes: fig-mpg we can then reference figure in our text as shown in @fig-mpg, heavier cars have lower mpg.
:::

#Table outputs

```{r}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| tbl-cap: "average mpg by cylinder count" 
#| echo: fenced

my_data %>% 
  group_by(cyl) %>% 
  summarise(avg_mpg = mean(mpg)) %>% 
  kable() #kable makes a clean markdown table
```

::: callout-tip
## Tip

this time we labeled the table above with the option #\| label: tbl-summary

we can reference in our text.

Please refer to @tbl-summary for the exact averages.

# Formulas with LaTeX

insert inline math equations with a single dollar sign: $y = mx + b$

for centered display equations, use double dollar signs: $$E = mc^2$$

# Common example equations

1.  Fractions $$
    \frac{1.5}{23}
    $$
2.  Super and Sub Scripts $$
    Y = x_1 + x_2
    $$ $$
    Y = x^1 + x^2
    $$
